Question: How hard is it for a Chinese speaker trying to understand Taiwanese?
Answer: Taiwanese languages are Austronesian, a different language family from Chinese. There are about forty languages and dialects extant, from Tayal (Squliq dialect) in the north, to Paiwan in the south. Unfortunately, only about 3% of the population of Taiwan knows a Taiwanese language. Very few people outside the tribes can say even a word from any of the Taiwanese languages. The vast majority of people in Taiwan speak one or more of three Chinese dialects: Mandarin, Minnan, and Hakka. If you know only Mandarin, Minnan is very difficult to understand at first, and then gradually you can pick things out. The same goes for Hakka, or any other Chinese dialect. They are variations on a theme, but the theme of Taiwanese languages is totally different. Mandarin comes from the north; Hakka and Minnan originally came from the north and contain many older elements. They have drifted so far apart that unless you get plenty of practice, they are unintelligible.
